description: Patch-level bumps of Duplicati are deliberately NOT automerged here, and the //patch-automerge preset is left out for four reasons that were measured rather than assumed.

First, there is nothing of that class to automerge. Of the 2667 tags linuxserver/duplicati publishes, strict semver leaves exactly six - 2.0.6, 2.0.7, 2.0.8, 2.1.0, 2.2.0 and 2.3.0 - and every bump since 2024 has been a minor one. `versioning=semver` on the annotation in defaults/main.yml is what keeps that list clean: the per-architecture and channel flavours (amd64-2.3.0, arm64v8-latest, 2.3.1-development) and the real upstream build tags (v2.3.0.4_stable_2026-07-09-ls305) are not semver, and Renovate's default docker versioning would read everything after the first dash as a compatibility suffix and quietly propose nothing at all.

Second, LinuxServer's three-component tag is not Duplicati's version. It carries Duplicati's first three components only; 2.3.0 is v2.3.0.4_stable_2026-07-09-ls305, and Duplicati's own patch level is the fourth component, which never reaches a tag Renovate can see. What Renovate would call a patch here - 2.0.7 to 2.0.8 - is a whole Duplicati release line, eleven months apart on the beta channel.

Third, Duplicati upgrades its settings database on startup, forward-only. Measured on this role's paths: a /config written by 2.2.0 and then started under 2.3.0 rewrites Duplicati-server.sqlite and leaves a `backup Duplicati-server <timestamp>.sqlite` beside it, and the 2.2.0 image afterwards refuses to start on that folder at all - `The database has version 11 but the largest supported version is 9` - with nothing listening on the port. Rolling back is a human restoring that file by hand. The one patch-class span that exists, 2.0.7 to 2.0.8, did not bump the schema and did downgrade cleanly, but that is a single data point about a class that has produced no release in two years, weighed against a program that holds the operator's only copy of their data.

Fourth, the pinned value does not identify an image in the first place. `2.3.0` is republished whenever LinuxServer rebuilds; it currently resolves to the same digest as `v2.3.0.4_stable_2026-07-09-ls305` and `latest`, and pointed at -ls304 a fortnight earlier. Since the role pulls with `pull: always`, operators already receive builds Renovate never proposed, so automerging the bumps it can see would not be the control it appears to be.

The Molecule scenario is strong enough that it would earn automerge if the above did not apply, and it is what a reviewer of a minor bump can lean on: it asserts the running server reports the pinned version on the stable channel, that /config, /backup and /source are bound to the role's host paths, that the API refuses unauthenticated requests and refuses `changeme` (the password the image falls back to when DUPLICATI__WEBSERVICE_PASSWORD is unset), and then creates a backup job over the API, runs it against a seeded canary file, clobbers the canary and restores it byte for byte.
